correctness.rationale: The binary 2-binomial equivalence lemma follows exactly from six length-at-most-two scattered counts. The suffix-extension recurrence is exact, prefix pruning at four square types is safe, and the complete breadth-first enumeration produces four states at length 43 and zero at 44. An independent direct-six-coordinate depth-first checker with complement symmetry reproduces the same extremizers and no depth 44 states; the four words are a single reversal/complementation orbit. Source programs are embedded in the package.

value.rationale: The paper motivating the question explicitly reports nonexistence of an infinite binary word with only three distinct 2-binomial squares. The exact largest finite word length 43 and complete extremizer classification sharply solve the resulting natural finite avoidance threshold, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a known-table recomputation. The finite bound makes the infinite obstruction quantitatively sharp and supplies explicit extremal words.
